title: Seaholm Vision, Budget, and Election Districts
summary:
*   Received updates on a visit to Austin's sister city, Orlu, Nigeria.
*   Reviewed a five-year financial forecast outlining the city's budget outlook.
*   Briefed on the proposed Master Plan for the future redevelopment of the Seaholm District.
*   Discussed a plan to divide the city into eight council districts for elections, though this redistricting proposal ultimately failed.
transcript:
MINUTES OF CITY COUNCIL WORKSESSION 
MAY 8,2002
Austin City Council
MINUTES
WORKESSION
WEDNESDAY, MAY 8, 2002
The following represents the actions taken by the Austin City Council in the order they
occurred during the meeting. While the minutes are not in sequential order, all agenda
items were discussed.
The City Council of Austin, Texas convened in a Work Session on Wednesday, May 8, 2002
at One Texas Center, 505 Barton Springs Road, third floor training room, Austin, Texas.
Mayor Garcia called the meeting to order at 10:14 a.m.
BRIEFINGS
1. 
Overview of Council Member Thomas' visit to Sister City, Orlu, Nigeria.
The presentation was made by Camille Donoghue, City of Austin's Sister Cities
Program Coordinator, Donetta Good all, Associate Vice President, Academic
Programs; and Beverly Silas, Vice Chair, Board of Directors, Austin Community
College; and Anhan Ogoh, Chairman, Austin Old-Orlu Sister Cities Committee.
2. 
Five-Year Budget Forecast.
The presentation was made by Rudy Garza, Assistant Director, Financial Services
3. 
Briefing on proposed Seaholm District Master Plan.
The presentation was made by Lisa Gordon, Assistant City Manager; Austan
Librach, Director, Planning, Transportation and Sustain ability; Jim Adams,
Electrical Control Systems Supervisor, Austin Energy; and Sherity Wagner,
Consultant, ROMA Design Group.
BRIEFING AND POSSIBLE ACTION
4. 
Discussion and possible action on the division of the city into eight council districts for the
election of councilmembers in the event that proposition 3 on the May 4, 2002, ballot is
approved by the voters.
No action required on this item because this proposition failed.
The motion to adjourn the meeting at 12:30 p.m. was approved on Council Member
Slusher's motion, Council Member second by a vote.

Mayor Pro Tern Goodman's second by a 6-0 vote. Council Member Thomas was off the
